title: Prove exact E8 root-low basis tariff 78 (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with an exact finite certificate, produced by Nick Petalas. For the fixed adjacent A8 roots v=(0,1), a=(0,2), the natural correction space `D=span(delta_a,E_a restricted to H_v)` has exact minimum reader-basis tariff **78** over every characteristic-zero field.

```text
29-neighbor root-low correction
  -> complete 511-character kernel table
  -> deficient words lie in three planes
  -> filtration dimensions 1,1,1,1,1,1,3,3,10
  -> exact basis profile (1,7,7,9,9,9,9,9,9,9)
```

Every basis has sorted weights at least that profile. The same basis therefore minimizes every nondecreasing tariff, with value `F(1)+2F(7)+7F(9)`. Under PR4052's singleton-encoder and exceptional-ray hypotheses, its strict-floor corollary gives **COPY >= 77** for this actual reader space. This is a lower bound, not an exact COPY optimum.

This answers one concrete candidate at conorholds' [PR4052](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4052) 29-neighbor opening. The source's threshold and COPY proofs are cited premises, not audited or replayed. Credit conorholds' PR3755/PR3166, DreamingOfClouds' decoder programme, adamgall's concave accounting and the retained E8 lineage. The new contribution is the explicit quotient classification and exact basis tariff. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

## Evidence

Before, PR4052 leaves mixed weight-seven reader directions beginning at 29 neighbor corrections outside its general 28-neighbor argument. After, this natural two-dimensional correction space has the exact profile above, and cannot reach the 72-unit baseline under the stated coupled model.

- All **511** nonzero character kernels agree with rational nullspace construction and a separate exact annihilation/modulo-101 rank certificate. The prime supplies a deterministic rational-rank lower bound, not a probabilistic inference.
- All seven nonempty unions of the three disjoint supports, the attaining ten-vector basis and seven failure/boundary controls pass. The universal coefficient and field quantifiers follow from the written kernel, disjoint-support and scalar-extension arguments.
- CPython **3.12.15**, macOS arm64, standard library only. Warning-strict normal and optimized direct runs pass, taking 1.35s and 1.18s in the recorded local check. Both registered commands passed locally and remain far below their 60-second limits. No performance improvement is claimed.
- `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` with declared source ancestry, and official six-file export integrity pass. Normal and optimized direct replays also pass in a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH; all exported files remain unchanged. An occupied receipt path is rejected.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/e8-root-low-plane/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/e8-root-low-plane/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/e8-root-low-plane
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/e8-root-low-plane --check-source-history
```

Other installations can substitute their CPython 3.12 path. Direct replay emits `PASS_E8_ROOT_LOW_PLANE` in a generated JSON receipt bound to all six package hashes; optional `--receipt PATH` creates a new receipt. No receipt is hand-written or committed.

## Limitations

Exactly one fixed correction space and root pair are covered. Arbitrary 29-site partial quotients, positive characteristics, masked targets and shared/dynamic delivery remain outside scope. The conditional COPY consequence retains the predecessor singleton classification and normalization premises. Physical access, restoration, native realization, compiler, stock, precision/tape and outer invoices remain open. All five selected framework assumptions remain. Selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, stronger unavailable static analyzers, independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

The current card is explicitly changed to this algebraic side result. Canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8 and selected PR6030 are recorded. Live overlap included 522 open PR records, 6,535 Discussion records, recent account contributions, targeted merged/main formula searches, and a fresh precommit delta. Sparse notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain limits.

## Open next questions

- Can a different correction space containing a 29-neighbor root-low word have basis tariff at most 72? Start by adjoining one independent correction and deriving its character-kernel filtration. No larger candidate or complete physical budget is supplied here.
- What is the exact coupled COPY optimum for this actual reader space? Start from the lower bound 77 and the source's exceptional-ray equations. An attaining factorization or stronger cut argument is missing.

- [PR3040](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3040) concerns rank-eight pattern rigidity after deletions. It does not price this corrected reader space.
- [PR5064](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5064) searches masked nine-factor completions. This proves an all-basis tariff for one explicit full-E8 ten-dimensional space, with no comparison of its search minima.
- [PR6569](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6569) accelerates PR3166's complete root-swap replay. This adds a new quotient result and does not change or rerun that scientific command.

- [PR6583](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6583) accelerates the orthogonal-core functional-section consumer. Its fixed section histogram differs from this corrected-space character-kernel filtration.
- [PR6584](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6584) accelerates the complete A2+E6 decoder replay. This result adds a quotient basis tariff and does not change or evaluate that decoder's COPY quantity.
